item.title: Cross-border workers for the grape harvest in Ticino: 15 francs an hour
item.description: In Ticino, 48 cross-border workers, mostly from the Varese area, work the grape harvest in the hills of Mendrisiotto. The net hourly pay is around 15 francs, with contracts lasting an average of a month and a half.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 48 cross-border workers pick and load the grapes - The pay is about 15 net francs per hour - The grape harvest generally lasts a month and a half - The day observed runs from 7 to 15, with a break
## Key facts - Location → Mendrisiotto hills - Team → 48 workers - Origin → mostly from the Varesotto area - Pay → about 15 net francs per hour - Grape harvest contract → generally a month and a half
At Mendrisio there are 48, among those who pick the grapes and those who load them, «all cross-border workers» coming mostly from the Varesotto area. The workers are busy on the hills of the Mendrisiotto; after the break they will return among the rows to finish the Merlot harvest, after a month of heat and hard work.
### A day among the rows
During the visit, scheduled for Tuesday, 29 September, it is 12:30. The grape harvesters are taking a break on folding chairs, after their packed lunch, before returning among the rows. Work started at 7; the break is scheduled between noon and 13, while the end is around 15. Alberto, 60, responsible for managing the work in several vineyards, explains, however, that there is no identical length for every day: depending on the vineyard and the work, one may stay for three hours or seven, eight.
The pay indicated by Alberto is «about fifteen net francs per hour». For the grape harvest alone, the contract generally lasts a month and a half. Those who work for the entire season are instead employed from April to November. Between those who pick and those who load, the group is therefore preparing to return to work to finish the harvest.
### Who makes up the group
The person in charge starts with the «hard core», that is, the people who return year after year, and adds the new applications received through the submission of résumés in Ticino. Broadly speaking, about ten new people arrive each year. The indicated age range is from 18 to 70. Alberto describes the team as consisting mainly of retirees or people who may have lost their jobs, while noting the presence of some young people.
The season was also affected by hail. In the areas hit, Alberto recounts, the damage was extensive, although the situation turned out to be less negative than expected. The grapes have a high alcohol content, linked to the concentration of sugars and the lack of rain. For the cross-border worker, the practical reality is a day marked by the break and the return among the rows. For the cross-border worker from the Varese area, the news offers a simple criterion for understanding vineyard work: distinguishing the duration of the assignment from that of the individual day. They are two separate variables. A month-and-a-half contract does not automatically mean identical hours every day, because Alberto links the hours to the vineyard and the work to be done.
### Two time frames not to confuse
| Commitment | Indicated duration | | Harvest | generally one and a half months | | Entire season | from April to November |
The hourly figure, about fifteen net francs, must therefore be considered together with the actual length of the workdays. A three-hour day and a seven- or eight-hour day produce different results; this is why the figure cannot be converted into a standard monthly salary using only the hourly rate. The day observed, from 7 until the break between noon and 13, with the expected finish around 15, is a concrete reference, but the same source points out that the organization varies from vineyard to vineyard.
The workers’ profile is also more varied than the definition of seasonal workers might suggest. Alberto speaks mainly of retirees and people who may have lost their jobs, but he also mentions some young people. The stated age range, from 18 to 70, therefore includes different experiences. According to the article, there are two ways to join the group: returning to the «hard core» or sending a résumé to Ticino, a route used by new applicants. Those seeking similar opportunities can start with annunci di lavoro, keeping the harvest period and the entire season distinct.
### Work beyond pay
The accounts of Maurizio and Matteo show two views of the job. Maurizio, retired after 43 years spent working in a factory as a lithographer, describes the vineyard as an outdoor activity, useful for meeting new people and enjoying a «pleasant distraction». Matteo, 52, from Varese, is working his fifteenth harvest in Ticino and his twenty-seventh overall. From his point of view, the change concerns the pace and atmosphere: what was once more festive is now more industrial and, in his words, «colder». For the cross-border worker, the comparison therefore concerns not only pay, but also duration, pace and working environment.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. To apply for the grape harvest in Ticino, the process indicated by the source can be organized into five steps. The starting point is the résumé; the rest concerns choosing the period, the age range, the schedule, and interpreting the pay.
### 1. Choosing the period
The first distinction is between the grape harvest, for which the contract generally lasts a month and a half, and work for the entire season, which runs from April to November. The application must therefore be consistent with one of the two durations.
### 2. Preparing the résumé
New applications are submitted by sending the résumé to Ticino. Those who return every year, on the other hand, are part of the «core group» contacted first by the person in charge. The source mentions about ten new people every year: this is the figure to keep in mind when assessing a new application.
### 3. Checking the age range
The stated age range is from 18 to 70 years. The team includes retirees, people who may have lost their jobs, and some young people; the profile is therefore not limited to a single category.
### 4. Clarifying the workday
Before estimating the commitment, bear in mind that a day may last three hours or seven or eight, depending on the vineyard and the work. The observed shift started at 7, included a break between noon and 13, and ended around 15. simulatore busta paga can help interpret the hourly figure without replacing the actual number of hours worked.
### 5. Understanding the pay correctly
The stated pay is approximately fifteen net francs per hour. Since the days can have different lengths, the total depends on the actual hours and the period chosen. To avoid a distorted comparison, it is advisable to use the hourly figure together with the expected schedule.
To estimate the net amount based on the expected hours, use calcolatore dello stipendio.

item.title: Living in Miazzina and working in Ticino as a cross-border commuter
item.description: New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement signed on 23 dicembre 2020 and in force from 1° gennaio 2024: rules, contributions and LAMal for those considering Miazzina.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Agreement signed on December 23, 2020 - In force since January 1, 2024 - Old cross-border workers: €7,500 exemption until 2033 - New cross-border workers: €10,000 allowance
## Key facts - Agreement → signed on December 23, 2020; in force since January 1, 2024 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13/6/2023 - Old cross-border workers → already such before 17/7/2023 - Exemption → €7,500; transitional regime 2024-2033 - New cross-border workers → €10,000 allowance - Withholding tax → deducted only in Switzerland - Double taxation → tax credit in section CE of the 730 form - LAMal → adult deductibles CHF 300-2,500
The New Cross-Border Worker Agreement was signed on December 23, 2020, and has been in force since January 1, 2024. For those considering living in Miazzina and working in the Canton of Ticino, 2026 is therefore not the effective date. Italy ratified the agreement with Law 83 of 13/6/2023.
### The rules that change the interpretation of income
The first step is to understand which category the cross-border worker falls into. Those who were already such before 17/7/2023 are considered 'old cross-border workers': for this group, the exemption is €7,500 and the transitional regime applies from 2024 to 2033. For new cross-border workers, the indicated allowance is instead €10,000. The date of one's status therefore comes before the calculation of the net salary and before choosing a home.
The principle indicated for the cross-border worker's employment income is precise: the deduction occurs only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation with a tax credit, to be managed in section CE of the 730 form. The system should not be described as taxation in both countries. The Double Taxation Convention between Italy and Switzerland was signed on March 9, 1976; Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member.
For the cross-border worker considering Miazzina, Italian residency and Ticino employment must therefore be read together with the applicable rule, not with a generic 'cross-border worker' label. The issue of tax refunds (ristorni) also appears in the framework to be prepared. The Italian declaration remains a separate step from the payroll deduction. These are operational differences: they change the way the payslip, the 730 form, and the comparison between gross and net are checked.
The administrative part is linked to the Permit G/B, while the tax framework remains tied to federal and cantonal laws and tax administrations. The choice of housing does not end with a percentage: the daily commute, travel times, cost of living, and the sustainability of the return must be placed alongside the available income. For Miazzina, this is the point to verify before turning the move into a final decision. The transition from gross to net income does not depend solely on withholding tax. The Swiss payslip includes social security contributions at different percentages, and part of the housing choice can change the monthly budget. For this reason, anyone considering Miazzina must simulate disposable income, rather than stopping at the salary stated in the offer.
### What is included in the net-income comparison
The AVS/AI/IPG share paid by the employee is 5.3%. For AD/AC, the rate is 1.1%, with a ceiling of CHF 148'200. LAINF is indicated at between 0.7% and 1.5%, while LPP varies from 7% to 18% depending on age bracket, starting at age 25. These figures have a tangible effect on how the payslip is read: the cross-border worker must identify each item before comparing a Ticino salary with the expenses incurred while living in Italy.
The second block concerns health coverage. The cross-border worker with a G permit has the right to opt for LAMal, i.e. health insurance. For adults, the deductibles indicated range from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. The decision must therefore be included in the personal budget together with commuting and housing, rather than treated as an undifferentiated item on the payslip.
A hypothetical case is enough to understand the method, without attributing unverified amounts or routes: if a cross-border worker chooses a home farther from the workplace, they must measure the effect of travel time and commuting expenses on the net amount already reduced by contributions and insurance. If the route passes through a border crossing such as Brogeda, the logistical verification remains separate from the tax calculation. The same criterion applies to the areas under consideration: first recurring expenses are compared, then it is decided whether the residual margin truly supports the move.
costo della vita should therefore be read together with the payslip, AVS, LPP and LAMal. It is the comparison that makes it possible to turn a salary difference into a concrete assessment, without confusing theoretical advantages with everyday costs.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the net salary calculator and the tax return guide. To turn the choice into a plan, the cross-border commuter can create a single worksheet for home, work, and taxes. The order matters because the date of the tax status and the reading of the payslip come before any comparison of living standards.
### Five checks before moving
1. Classify your status. Check whether you were already a cross-border commuter before 17/7/2023. This step determines the old or new cross-border commuter category, the €7'500 exemption under the 2024-2033 transitional regime, or the €10'000 allowance.
2. Establish the legal timeline. The New Cross-Border Commuters Agreement was signed on 23/12/2020, has been in force since 1° gennaio 2024, and Italian ratification is Law 83 of 13/6/2023. Do not use 2026 as the start date.
3. Separate withholding from the tax return. Employment income tax is withheld only in Switzerland. To avoid double taxation, the tax credit must be entered in section CE of form 730. The Italy-Switzerland Convention was signed on 9 marzo 1976.
4. Review all the Swiss items. Check AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3%, AD/AC at 1.1% up to the CHF 148'200 limit, LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%, and LPP between 7% and 18% starting with the 25-year age bracket. For the tax side, federal and cantonal rates are established by federal and cantonal laws and administered by AFC/ESTV and the cantonal tax administrations, not by BFS or UFAS.
5. Complete the health and budget section. For the G permit, include the LAMal right of option and consider adult deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. Then compare the net amount with housing costs, the route, and the border crossings assessed before deciding.
For the Italian reading of IRPEF rates, the source indicates, from 2026, 23% up to €28'000, 33% from €28'001 to €50'000, and 43% above €50'000, according to Law 199/2025, art. 1 c. 3; for 2024-2025 income, it indicates 23%, 35%, and 43%. This overview does not change the Swiss withholding rule: it serves to keep the years and references separate when preparing the tax documentation.
After these checks, use the calcolatore stipendio to estimate the net amount and compare it with your relocation budget.

item.title: Living in Craveggia and working in Ticino as a cross-border worker
item.description: New Cross-Border Workers Agreement: signed on December 23, 2020, in force from January 1, 2024, with different exemptions for old and new cross-border workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The New Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020 - Entry into force: 1 January 2024 - Old frontier workers: €7,500 exemption - New frontier workers: €10,000 allowance
## Key facts - Employment income tax → withheld only in Switzerland - Tax credit in Italy → Section CE of the 730 form - Old frontier workers → transitional regime 2024-2033 - Italy-Switzerland Convention → 9 March 1976 - IRPEF from 2026 → 23%, 33%, 43% - AVS/AI/IPG → 5.3% paid by the employee - AD/AC → 1.1% up to CHF 148'200 - LAMal → right of option for frontier workers with a G permit
## The starting framework The New Agreement on frontier workers was signed on 23 December 2020, ratified in Italy by Law 83 of 13 June 2023 and has been in force since 1 January 2024. For people living in Craveggia and working in Ticino as frontier workers, this sequence of dates is the reference for understanding the tax treatment before considering a move.
The correct date is not 2026: the phrase 2026 new tax agreement does not describe when the agreement entered into force. The operative step was 1 January 2024. The decisive distinction instead concerns 17 July 2023. Anyone who was already a frontier worker before that date belongs to the old frontier-worker category: an exemption of €7,500 and a transitional regime from 2024 to 2033 apply to them. New frontier workers have a €10,000 allowance.
### Withholding tax and double taxation For frontier workers, tax on employment income is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit indicated in Section CE of the 730 form: the tax return must therefore be read together with the Swiss withholding, not as a second identical charge. For the filing step, the operational reference is the income tax return.
The Italy-Switzerland Convention against double taxation was signed on 9 March 1976. The framework must also be read in light of the fact that Switzerland is neither a member of the European Union nor of the European Economic Area. These are the basic facts to keep in view, without confusing residence in Craveggia with the place of work in Canton Ticino. ## From regulation to the payslip
For a cross-border worker, the choice to live in Craveggia and work in Ticino does not end with the tax allowance. The practical check starts with the payslip, where withholding tax and social contributions have different functions. Separating the items prevents amounts that the source assigns to the Swiss system from being attributed to Italian IRPEF.
### Swiss deductions to review
| Item | Indicated data | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5,3% borne by the employee | | AD/AC | 1,1%, capped at CHF 148'200 | | LAINF | between 0,7% and 1,5% | | LPP | between 7% and 18% by age bracket, from the 25° year onward |
AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF, and LPP are not a single deduction. The available data indicate separate rates: the first is 5,3% for the employee; the second is 1,1% up to the limit of CHF 148'200; LAINF ranges from 0,7% to 1,5%; LPP ranges from 7% to 18% by age bracket starting at age 25. An orderly review of the payslip starts here, without adding different percentages together as if they were a single item.
Italian taxation also changes by year. From 2026, IRPEF is indicated at 23% up to 28.000 euros, at 33% between 28.001 and 50.000 euros, and at 43% above 50.000 euros. For 2024-2025 income, the reported rates are 23%, 35%, and 43%. Comparing them with the Swiss deduction therefore requires keeping years and mechanisms separate.
The rates of federal and cantonal withholding tax are established by federal and cantonal laws. At the federal level, they are administered by AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations are also involved. They are not rates set by UFAS or BFS. As regards residence and work, the G permit and Canton Ticino remain the practical framework for the review. When choosing a place of residence, travel times, housing costs, and area should be treated as separate checks: they cannot be inferred from the rates. A border crossing such as Brogeda belongs to this logistical check, to be considered alongside the tax check. For comparison, costo della vita Ticino vs Italia and tempi di attesa ai valichi can be used. ## Checklist before moving
Before deciding whether to live in Craveggia and work in Ticino, it is advisable to turn the rules into an orderly check. The following process starts with the dates, rates and procedures referenced by the source.
### 1. Establish the tax category
Start from the date of 17 luglio 2023. If you were already a cross-border worker before that date, the reference is the 7.500 euro exemption with the 2024-2033 transitional regime. If you fall among new cross-border workers, consider the 10.000 euro allowance. Do not replace these two positions with the date of the move alone: the criterion provided is whether you were a cross-border worker before or after 17 luglio 2023.
### 2. Align withholding and tax return
Note the agreement's three dates: signed on 23 dicembre 2020, ratified by Italy with Law 83 on 13 giugno 2023, entered into force on 1° gennaio 2024. Then check that employment income has withholding tax deducted only in Switzerland. In Italy, the tax credit is entered via box CE of the 730. This is the step to use for double taxation and for dichiarazione dei redditi.
### 3. Review social security and healthcare items
Check AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP separately, applying the available figures: 5,3%, 1,1% up to CHF 148'200, 0,7-1,5% and 7-18% by age bracket from the 25° year. On the healthcare side, cross-border workers with permit G have the right to choose LAMal; the deductibles indicated for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500.
### 4. Keep commuting and taxes separate
Connections, travel times, cost of living and recommended areas should not be inferred from tax rates. Even when considering a border crossing such as Brogeda, the logistical check is separate from the tax one. For the final comparison between residence and work, use comparatore Permesso G vs B and then measure the effect on the payslip with calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Varese-Ticino agreement: S40/S50 every 30 min and RE50 to Malpensa
item.description: The Regional Council has ratified the agreement: S40 and S50 every 30 min between Varese and Mendrisio. The RE50 for Malpensa and Lugano is planned.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Green light for ratification between Lombardy and Canton Ticino - S40 and S50: Varese-Mendrisio every thirty minutes - RE50 planned between Malpensa, Varese and Lugano - S30: Cadenazzo-Luino-Gallarate to be strengthened
## Key facts What → new agreement on cross-border mobility Railway network → S40, S50, S30 and prospect of RE50 Service → integrated connection every thirty minutes between Varese and Mendrisio Next step → meeting with the councillor at the session on October 1 Tickets → Swiss tickets, Io Viaggio and Io Viaggio in Famiglia on the Como-Varese corridor Study → former Castellanza-Malnate Olona-Mendrisio railway
The Regional Council gave the green light to ratifying the new agreement between Lombardy and Canton Ticino for the development of cross-border mobility. The measure directly concerns the Varese area, affected every day by travel to Switzerland and connections with the Malpensa area.
Its significance is underscored by Giuseppe Licata, regional councillor and vice-president of the Special Committee «Enhancement and protection of mountain and border areas; Relations between Lombardy and the Swiss Confederation». For Licata, the agreement must make the mobility system more integrated and offer cross-border commuters and other citizens concrete alternatives to the private car. The province of Varese, located between Lombardy, Canton Ticino and Malpensa, is identified as one of the network's central points.
### The planned routes
Rail consolidation centers on the S40 and S50 lines. The source indicates that they will continue to connect Varese with Mendrisio, Como, Lugano and Bellinzona, ensuring an integrated service every thirty minutes between Varese and Mendrisio. The planning also includes the prospect of the RE50 Malpensa-Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano, designed to improve the connection between the Varese area, Ticino and the airport.
For the Upper Varese area, the agreement provides for work on the S30 Cadenazzo-Luino-Gallarate line, with the aim of progressively increasing frequencies and connections. Licata asks that Varese remain a leading player in the subsequent phases and that the objectives become concrete and reliable services. He also requested that a meeting with the councillor be scheduled to discuss developments and implementation: the session is already scheduled for October 1.
The section is not limited to trains. New bus connections are planned in the border areas between the provinces of Varese and Como, along with coordination between road and rail services and completion of the range of cross-border tickets and season passes. On the Como-Varese corridor, the agreement also provides for mutual recognition, at least on certain routes or services, of some Swiss tickets and the Lombardy regional passes Io Viaggio and Io Viaggio in Famiglia.
Rounding out the picture is the study of the former Castellanza-Malnate Olona-Mendrisio railway. The scenarios outlined include rail reactivation, tram solutions and cycling infrastructure. To follow the day-to-day aspect of travel, the agreement can be read alongside the guide to mezzi pubblici Ticino. ## The practical perspective for cross-border commuters
For those who work across the border, the agreement should be read as a network of connected corridors. The source does not concentrate the measures on a single route: it brings together S40, S50, S30, the prospect of RE50, buses, travel tickets and the study on the former railway. The concrete impact will therefore depend on the corridor used by the commuter and the type of service involved.
### Four corridors, four effects
| Corridor | Measure indicated | What it means for travelers | |---|---|---| | Varese-Mendrisio | S40 and S50, with integrated service every thirty minutes | Rail alternative to the private car | | Malpensa-Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano | Prospect of RE50 | Planned connection to the airport | | Cadenazzo-Luino-Gallarate | Development of S30 and a gradual increase in frequencies and connections | Measure aimed at Alto Varesotto | | Como-Varese | Recognition of certain tickets on specific routes or services | More coordinated cross-border offering |
This distinction helps prevent different measures from being read in the same way. S40 and S50 are described as lines that will continue to connect Varese with Mendrisio, Como, Lugano and Bellinzona. For RE50, on the other hand, the source speaks of a prospect incorporated into planning. In the case of S30, the goal is a gradual increase. On the Como-Varese corridor, the practical point is the mutual recognition of certain Swiss and Lombard tickets, not a blanket reference to all services.
For the commuter traveling along the Varese-Mendrisio corridor, the most precise reference is therefore the integrated frequency indicated in the agreement. For those whose connection point is Malpensa, the element to follow is the prospect of RE50. In Alto Varesotto, attention is instead focused on the development of line S30 and the gradual increase in connections.
The section on buses and fares adds another layer. The agreement indicates new connections in the border areas between Varese and Como, along with coordination between road and rail transport. For a cross-border commuter, this means considering mobility not only on the basis of an individual line, but also the possibility of connecting different services and checking the scope of the recognized tickets. Comparison of alternatives to the private vehicle can be supplemented by the tool on costo auto pendolare.
The former Castellanza-Malnate Olona-Mendrisio railway also becomes part of this overall vision. The study mentioned by the source is not limited to a single solution: it considers railway reactivation, trams and cycling infrastructure. For Licata, rail, buses, interchange, fares and connections with Malpensa must be addressed through a cross-territorial approach, because they affect the daily lives of citizens and workers.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From the news to daily monitoring
For a cross-border commuter or a commuter, following implementation means distinguishing the connection of interest from the measure concerning it. The text of the agreement makes it possible to set up a four-step check, without confusing a rail service, a planning outlook and a study of the right-of-way.
### Four operational steps
1. Start from the reference corridor. Consider whether the journey concerns Varese-Mendrisio and the onward routes toward Como, Lugano or Bellinzona, the connection with Malpensa, the Upper Varese area or the Como-Varese corridor.
2. Classify the measure. For S40 and S50, the source refers to connections that will continue and to an integrated service every thirty minutes between Varese and Mendrisio. For RE50 and S30, by contrast, identify a planning perspective and a goal of gradual increase, respectively.
3. When assessing buses and travel tickets, focus the check on the border areas between the provinces of Varese and Como and on the routes or services covered by the recognition. The agreement mentions some Swiss tickets, Io Viaggio and Io Viaggio in Famiglia along the Como-Varese corridor.
4. Note the first institutional step indicated in the text: Licata has requested a meeting with the councillor to examine developments and implementation in greater depth, already scheduled for the session on primo ottobre. This is the explicit time reference linked to the next phase of the agreement.
This sequence makes it possible to follow the news without conflating different levels. The rail connection, integration with buses, recognition of tickets and the study of the former railway right-of-way in fact have different functions within the same agreement. For those who work in Canton Ticino, the point to keep separate is the everyday corridor from the scenario concerning future planning.
The Castellanza-Malnate Olona-Mendrisio line requires a separate check: the study will have to identify possible scenarios involving railway reactivation, tramway solutions and cycling infrastructure. On the services front, however, the criterion indicated by Licata is to turn objectives into concrete and reliable connections, with greater coordination between rail and bus services.
To find your way among the travel options, consult mezzi pubblici Ticino.

item.title: Ticino LAMal premiums 2027: increase to 3,7% and 519,90 francs
item.description: In 2027, the increase in premiums in Ticino will be 3,7%, with 519,90 francs per month. DSS Director Raffaele De Rosa comments on the measures and healthcare spending.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 3,7%: increase in Ticino premiums in 2027 - 5%: national average for 2027 - 519,90 francs per month: the figure indicated for Ticino - Moratoriums: measurable effect, but an imperfect tool
## Key facts - Person responsible→Raffaele De Rosa, director of the DSS - Sector under review→physiotherapy - Measure announced→systematic survey shortly - Training→SUPSI: around thirty; Ludes: approximately 240 graduates annually
In 2027, the average increase in health insurance premiums in Ticino is indicated at 3,7%, compared with 5% nationally. For the first time in years, the increase in Ticino therefore remains below the Swiss average. However, this result does not change the Canton’s position: at 519,90 francs per month, it continues to record the highest premiums in the Confederation.
Raffaele De Rosa, director of the Department of Health and Social Affairs, the DSS, commented on the figures in an interview with SEIDISERA. His remarks combine concern about the burden on families with a determination to continue with moratoriums and blanket checks. For the cross-border worker employed in Ticino, the concrete connection offered by the source is the cost of LAMal in the Canton; guida sulla LAMal may be the entry point for remaining solely on the healthcare topic. The interview does not address taxation or social security.
De Rosa links the increase to the overall rise in healthcare spending. His analysis includes the number of providers, including doctors, specialists and healthcare facilities, the cost of medicines, the volume of services, medical progress with more expensive innovative treatments, and demographic ageing. To these factors he adds misguided system incentives: in LAMal, he explained, in many areas more services provided or prescribed can translate into higher earnings, creating vicious circles.
The 3,7% therefore brings no personal satisfaction. De Rosa spoke of concern and frustration over the work carried out by the Canton.
> «Personally, I feel no satisfaction whatsoever».
### Measures already implemented
The director of the DSS cited every remaining margin allowed by federal law: the freeze in eight medical specialties, the freeze concerning private Spitex services and home nurses, the reduction of the tariff point for outpatient medical services, and health-promotion programmes. His conclusion is that curbing the growth of healthcare spending and premiums is possible, but that efforts must be intensified to bring the rates back to more bearable levels.
According to De Rosa, the moratoriums have already produced tangible and measurable results in containing spending, with a direct impact on premiums. However, they remain a powerful yet imperfect tool because they do not act directly on the overall volume of services.
The physiotherapy sector is now under review: spending is growing far above the Swiss average. A systematic survey to map the sector will be launched shortly; the proposed solutions also include promoting outpatient flat-rate payments. Finally, there is training: SUPSI graduates around thirty students a year, Ludes approximately 240. De Rosa calls for reflection on the overall model and the Canton’s actual needs. The percentage figure and the monthly amount tell two different stories. For those who work across the border and incur costs linked to Ticino, 3.7% may seem like a slowdown compared to the 5% national average; however, this is not a decrease in spending. The 59.90 Swiss francs per month remain the benchmark that prevents interpreting the figure as a problem already solved. The cost of living comparison can help place this amount alongside other expenses, without attributing meanings to it that the interview does not provide.
### A partial brake
The merit of the moratoriums, according to De Rosa, is measurable: they contain spending and directly impact premiums. The limitation is equally clear: they do not act directly on the overall volume of services. If the volume of care, the price of medicines, the number of providers, and medical progress continue to drive spending, the freeze remains a partial tool. This is why the director of the DSS defines it as incisive yet imperfect and calls for intensified efforts.
The proposal for outpatient lump sums is presented as a way out of the logic whereby those who prescribe or provide more treatments earn much more. De Rosa's analysis thus shifts the focus from the final premium number alone to the incentives that influence volumes.
### Cantonal and federal
Canton Ticino has acted with rigor, pioneering freezes that other cantons have taken as a model. But the fundamental rules remain federal: the catalog of reimbursed services and drug prices depend on Bern. For a cross-border worker, this distinction clarifies why a cantonal measure and a federal reform do not have the same scope of action.
The scope must be kept tight. The source does not address the G permit, OASI, LPP, tax rebates, withholding tax, or double taxation. It therefore offers no elements to attribute effects to the 3.7% on these dossiers: the link to the cross-border worker remains limited to the health insurance issue of LAMal in Canton Ticino.
The political landscape is widening: in Federal Councillor Baume-Schneider's press conference, concerns shared even north of the Alps emerged. De Rosa observes that other cantons are beginning to experience similar difficulties; hence the hope for alliances for necessary reforms. At the same time, the distance between about thirty SUPSI graduates and about 240 Ludes graduates brings us back to the canton's actual personnel needs: this is not data on premiums, but a sign of the overall model to be evaluated.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. To turn the interview into a practical check, the cross-border reader can use a sequence limited to the available data. No inferences about permits or taxes are needed: the source concerns premiums, healthcare spending, moratoriums, physiotherapy and training. The aim is to distinguish what is already indicated from what has merely been announced.
### Reading checklist
1. Start with the monthly figure. Record 519,90 francs as the reference for Ticino. Do not replace it with a different average: it is the amount indicated by the source for comparing the burden.
2. Put the rates side by side. Write 3,7% for the average increase in Ticino in 2027 and 5% for the national average. The column serves to show the growth, not to erase the monthly level.
3. Separate the measures. Keep the measures cited by De Rosa in one section and the physiotherapy census announced shortly in another. This way you do not confuse a measure already mentioned with a future action.
4. Identify the decision-making level. Moratoriums and inspections are the responsibility of the Canton; the catalogue of reimbursed services and the price of medicines, on the other hand, depend on the federal rules specified in the interview.
The passage on physiotherapy merits a separate check. When the systematic census is launched, the sector can be assessed through precise mapping, which De Rosa presents as a basis for obtaining an overview of the sector. However, the source does not provide a more specific date, a form or an individual request to submit: it is not correct to invent a procedure.
The same criterion applies to training. The comparison between SUPSI and Ludes is not presented as a verdict on a single institution, but as a reason to question the adequacy of the model in relation to the Canton’s actual needs. For the cross-border reader, it is a signal to follow in terms of healthcare decisions, not proof of an already-defined personal impact.
To explore the healthcare side alone in greater depth, consult guida all'assicurazione malattia LAMal. To measure the effect of the monthly cost on employment income, use calcolatore fiscale dello stipendio.

## In brief - The Regional Council ratifies the Lombardy-Ticino Agreement - Agreement signed on 16 June 2026: lasts five years - Services scheduled every 60 minutes: S40 and S50 - RE50 Malpensa-Lugano and new cross-border buses planned
## Key facts - Bill → no. 197 - Agreement → signed on 16 June 2026 - Validity → five years, renewable for another five - S40 and S50 → frequency every 60 minutes - Varese-Mendrisio service → integrated every 30 minutes - RE50 → Malpensa-Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano, hourly frequency - S30 → Cadenazzo-Luino-Gallarate - Fares → goal of integration between the Lombardy and Ticino systems
### An agreement that starts in the Varese area The Regional Council approved Bill no. 197, which ratifies the new Agreement between Regione Lombardia and Canton Ticino for the development of cross-border mobility. The agreement was signed on 16 June 2026 and will be valid for five years, with the possibility of renewal for an additional five-year period.
For the province of Varese, the measure is directly relevant: the area is affected by daily travel to Switzerland and by connections between Ticino, Malpensa and the Lombardy railway network. For cross-border commuters, the stated objective is to offer concrete alternatives to private cars, with more coordinated, accessible and efficient rail and road-based services. The practical reference therefore becomes the mezzi pubblici Ticino network.
Giuseppe Licata, regional councillor and vice-president of the Special Committee «Enhancement and protection of mountain and border areas; Relations between Lombardy and the Swiss Confederation», described the Agreement as an important step for Varese and called for the area to play a leading role in the next phases. The priorities identified include Malpensa, the Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano axis and the Luino corridor.
### The railway network and new connections The Agreement considers the system formed by the S10, S40 and S50 lines, which connects Bellinzona, Lugano, Chiasso, Como and Varese via the Mendrisio hub. Medium-term planning confirms the S40 Varese-Mendrisio-Como and the S50 Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano-Bellinzona-Biasca, both with a frequency of every 60 minutes. Between Varese and Mendrisio, the integrated service is scheduled every 30 minutes.
For the Varese area, the RE50 Malpensa-Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano is also indicated, with hourly frequency and stops, among others, at Malpensa Terminal 1, Busto Arsizio, Gallarate, Varese and Mendrisio. The Verbano and Upper Varese corridor is instead connected to the S30 Cadenazzo-Luino-Gallarate. The agreement also provides for new bus connections in the border areas of the provinces of Varese and Como and the coordination of road-based lines with railway routes. A permanent Technical Working Group between Regione Lombardia, Cantone Ticino and Agenzia per il TPL del bacino di Como, Lecco e Varese is also planned. ## The network as a decision-making tool
The practical value indicated by the Agreement lies not in a single route, but in the connection between rail, buses, interchanges, fares, and Malpensa. For a cross-border commuter from the province of Varese, Mendrisio is the reference point for understanding the network: from here, routes toward Como, Lugano, Bellinzona, Biasca, and Malpensa can be considered. The plan therefore concerns different destinations and not just one connection.
### Three horizons for frequencies
The source distinguishes between medium-term planning, planned service, and long-term objectives. This distinction is useful for correctly interpreting the indications: S40 and S50 belong to medium-term planning, RE50 is presented as a planned service, while for S30 the text separates the medium-term frequencies from the long-term target.
| Route | Indication | Practical interpretation | | S40 and S50 | 60 minutes; every 30 minutes between Varese and Mendrisio | shared corridor as far as Mendrisio | | RE50 | hourly frequency | connection also intended for Malpensa | | S30 | 120 minutes Cadenazzo-Luino; 60 minutes Luino-Gallarate; target of 60 minutes over the entire route | development in phases |
For those based in Alto Varesotto, the S30 therefore has a different service pattern depending on the segment. The figures given for Cadenazzo-Luino and Luino-Gallarate describe a non-uniform service pattern in the medium term; the subsequent objective is to bring the frequency to 60 minutes across the entire service span and the entire route.
### Buses and tickets in the same plan
The Agreement provides for new bus connections in the border areas around Varese and Como and the coordination of road-based lines with rail lines. For a cross-border commuter, this must therefore be understood as a combination of modes, not as an isolated choice of train.
The same logic appears in fares: completing the range of cross-border tickets and passes, further integrating rail and road transport, and combining the Lombardy fare system with the Ticino one. The Agreement also envisages the mutual recognition, at least on certain routes or services, of certain Swiss tickets and the Lombardy regional passes Io Viaggio and Io Viaggio in Famiglia on the Como-Varese corridor. Anyone comparing public transport with the car can supplement the analysis by using the costo auto pendolare.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## From reading to action
For a cross-border commuter who wants to follow the implementation of the Agreement, it is useful to separate the rail route, any bus segment, fares and the political level. This distinguishes the planned service, medium-term planning and the long-term objective.
### Five steps to find your bearings
1. Identify the route. Associate your mobility with S40, on the Varese-Mendrisio-Como route, with S50, on the Varese-Mendrisio-Lugano-Bellinzona-Biasca route, with RE50, between Malpensa and Lugano, or with S30, between Cadenazzo, Luino and Gallarate. This clarifies which axis of the Agreement to follow.
2. Mark the time horizon. Next to the line, note whether the source refers to medium-term planning, a planned service or a long-term objective. For S30, also distinguish Cadenazzo-Luino from Luino-Gallarate: the indicated frequencies are not the same.
3. Verify intermodality. When following implementation, look for the connection between the new buses in the border areas and the rail routes. The point to follow is the coordination between rail and road transport provided for by the agreement.
4. Read the fares together with the stated condition. The objective concerns cross-border tickets and passes, integration between the Lombard and Ticinese systems and the possible mutual recognition, on certain routes or services, of Swiss passes and Io Viaggio and Io Viaggio in Famiglia on the Como-Varese corridor. Do not automatically extend this provision to every route.
5. Follow the institutional steps. Giuseppe Licata, vice-president of the Special Commission for Mountain Areas, has requested a meeting with the councillor to examine developments and concrete implementation in greater depth; the session has already been scheduled for Thursday 1 October. The funded study on the former Castellanza-Malnate Olona-Mendrisio railway is also part of this monitoring, aimed at identifying a strategy for using the railway right-of-way, while assessing trams, an interconnected railway and cycling infrastructure.
This framework helps you read future updates without confusing a planning decision with a service that is already available. To complete your personal commuting planning, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: LAMal, 30 years of increases: premiums have tripled
item.description: LAMal, introduced in 1996, has seen the average premium triple. For 2027, the DFI indicates +5% in Switzerland and +3.7% in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - LAMal introduced on 1 January 1996 - Average premiums tripled in over 30 years - 2027: +5% in Switzerland and +3.7% in Ticino - In Ticino adults over 600 CHF per month
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | Introduction | 1 January 1996 | | Increase in children | 170% | | Young adult increase | 179% | | Adult increase | 190% | | National average increase 2027 | 5% | | Increase in Ticino 2027 | 3.7% | | Adults in Ticino in 2027 | just over CHF 600 per month | | Young adults in Ticino in 2027 | about CHF 418 per month |
January 1, 1996 is the date of introduction of LAMal, the Federal Health Insurance Act. Almost 31 years have passed since this law regulates compulsory basic health insurance for all persons residing in Switzerland.
LAMal defines the insurance obligation and the basic coverage. Thelatter guarantees access to essential medical care and covers the costs of illness, accident and maternity. The law also regulates the private management of recognised insurance and the equality of the benefits provided by all health insurance funds. For an overview of the assicurazione LAMal, these are the items to keep separate from the prize data alone.
In over 30 years, however, the average monthly premium has tripled. The graphical processing cited in the source distinguishes the trend by age: the increase was 170% for children, 179% for young adults and 190% for adults. The comparison between the national 5% and the Ticino 3.7% may seem favorable, but the text highlights a second element: premium levels in Ticino remain the highest in all the categories considered. The difference between the two increases, therefore, does not erase the premium data indicated by the source for adults, young adults and minors.
The analysis also requires distinguishing the period observed. On the one hand, there is the series spanning more than 30 years, during which the average monthly premium tripled and the increases by age were 170%, 179% and 190%. On the other hand, there is the update for 2027 alone, with the national average at 5% and Ticino at 3.7%. Mixing the two measures would lead to interpreting as an annual variation a figure that the source presents over a much longer period.
### What can be said to the cross-border worker
For a cross-border worker, the scope must be kept clear. The source discusses LAMal as compulsory basic health insurance for people residing in Switzerland and quantifies premiums in Ticino. It does not, however, describe the position of those living across the border and provides no data on G permit, AVS, LPP, withholding tax or INPS. Nor does it address the new 2026 tax agreement or double taxation.
This limitation does not make the figures useless, but it prevents attributing a specific effect to them on the cross-border worker's payslip, taxation or social security. The source does not in fact indicate a relationship between the premiums mentioned and these topics. For a separate comparison between Swiss and Italian expenses, costo della vita Ticino vs Italia can be used, without turning the LAMal figure into a tax or social-security rule.
The practical reading therefore remains limited: the change projected for 2027 is lower in Ticino than the national average, while the monthly amounts in Ticino are indicated as the highest for all age groups. This is the central tension described by the source.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. The text makes it possible to build a reading sheet without adding external data. The first step is to separate the history of LAMal from the 2027 projection; the second is to keep the national average distinct from the value referring to Ticino.
### Four data checks
1. Identify the age group. The source distinguishes children, young adults and adults in the series of increases, while for 2027 it indicates adults, young adults and minors. 2. Note the correct measure. For 2027, the national reference is the average increase of 5%; for Ticino it is 3.7%. These are percentage increases, not monthly amounts. 3. Separate percentage and premium. The Ticino amounts reported are just over 600 CHF per month for adults, around 418 CHF for young adults and 153 CHF for minors. 4. Preserve the time reference. Growth since 2024 is described as continuous for all age groups; the historical figure of over 30 years, on the other hand, concerns the tripling of the average premium.
This sequence avoids the main reading error: using 5% or 3.7% as if they were the premium to be paid, or using the 2027 monthly values as if they were a measure valid for every category. The source does not indicate a specific health insurer, a deductible, a subsidy, an administrative deadline or an individual amount different from those reported. It is therefore not possible to derive a more detailed personal procedure from this text.
For those working in Ticino, the possible check using only the source consists of recording the relevant category and comparing the two levels of increase, keeping the national data and the Ticino data separate. Anyone wishing to supplement this reading with a calculation for their own budget can consult calcolatore dello stipendio.

item.title: Ticino health insurance premiums 2027: 3,7% increase
item.description: In 2027, health insurance premiums in Ticino increase by 3,7%, bringing the average premium to 520 francs per month, the highest in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - In 2027, health insurance premiums in Ticino will increase by 3,7%. - The national average for next year is 5%. - The average Ticino premium reaches almost 520 francs. - Jura records 6,6%; Glarus 3%.
## Key facts Year → 2027 Increase in Ticino → 3,7% National average → 5% Average Ticino premium → 520 francs per month Average increase → 18,6 francs Previous average premium → 501,3 francs per month Highest increase → Jura, 6,6% Smallest increase → Glarus, 3%
In 2027, health insurance premiums in the Canton of Ticino will increase by 3,7%, after years in which increases hovered around 10% and the Canton almost always remained among those hardest hit. The increase expected for next year is therefore slightly below the national average of 5%.
For the cross-border worker reader, the key point is territorial: the source provides a snapshot of the Canton of Ticino, that is, the Canton at the center of the news, but does not break down premiums by insured category. It therefore does not indicate a specific rate for those crossing the border. The usable figure remains the cantonal one, referring to the average premium.
The difference between percentage and francs is the crux of the news. The 3,7% indicates growth compared with the previous year, while the 18,6 francs show the average monthly increase. The two measures describe the same development from different angles and explain why a percentage increase below average does not coincide with the lowest average premium.
### The figure concerning the Canton
The figures provided by the Federal Office of Public Health and the Ticino Department of Health and Social Affairs bring the average Ticino premium to 520 francs per month, the highest level in Switzerland. The percentage change is more contained than in previous years, but the change in francs is an average of 18,6 francs: the premium rises from 501,3 francs per month last year to almost 520 next year.
Comparison with the other Cantons puts the result into perspective. Jura records the strongest increase, at 6,6%, while Glarus stands at 3%, the lowest figure. The Swiss average of 5% places Ticino below the national threshold in percentage terms, without changing its position as the canton with the highest average premium.
Those who work in Ticino and read these figures from the cross-border worker perspective therefore find two different pieces of information: annual growth is lower than average, while the average amount remains the highest. To explore the topic further, one can consult confronto sull'assicurazione malattia, keeping the general cantonal figure separate from any individual situation. ## Age groups and cost items
The 3,7% indicated for Canton Ticino does not by itself describe all age groups. The source distinguishes adults, young adults and children, associating each category with a change and an average premium.
| Age group | Change | Average premium | |---|---:|---:| | Adults, age 26 and over | 3,7% | 603,6 francs | | Young adults, 19-25 years | 3,5% | 418,4 francs | | Children, up to 18 years | 3,4% | 153,2 francs |
The highest figure applies to adults, with an average premium of 603,6 francs. For young adults, the average premium is 418,4 francs, while for children it drops to 153,2 francs. The percentage change varies little among the three groups: 3,7% for adults, 3,5% for young adults and 3,4% for children.
For the cross-border commuter reader, this is the most concrete reading available: not a tariff based on the border, but three references arranged by age. The text does not add a specific breakdown for cross-border commuters; the distinction presented remains the age-based one.
### The composition of healthcare costs
The second block of data concerns the items that affect costs. Hospitals, including outpatient and inpatient care, account for 32%; followed by medical practices at 23% and medicines at 18%. Nursing homes account for 7%, while physiotherapy and Spitex each account for 5%. Laboratories account for 3%, and the item indicated as psychotherapy psychology accounts for 2%.
The breakdown places hospitals first among the reported items, followed by medical practices and medicines. To read the data correctly, it is advisable to consider the age group and cost structure together, without turning a cantonal average into a personal amount. confronto sulla cassa malati may accompany this reading, but the source values remain average reference values for Canton Ticino.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From the news to a verification
The most appropriate way to use the news is to treat it as a comparison sheet, not as an individual quote. The only time horizon indicated is next year, identified in the text as 2027; no other operational deadlines are provided.
### Five steps for reading the data
1. **Set the year**: start from 2027, which is the reference indicated for the next increase in premiums in Canton Ticino. 2. Identify the age bracket: separate adults aged 26 and over, young adults between 19 and 25 years old, and children up to 18 years old, without mixing the three average values. 3. Compare percentages and francs: Canton Vaud records an increase of 4.5% and an average rise of 13.7 francs; Zug records 4.4% and 11.6 francs. The two pairs show why the percentage and the monthly amount are different measures. 4. Keep the cantonal level: the figure for Canton Ticino concerns an average premium. The source does not present a personal rate or a figure specific to a cross-border worker. 5. Check the correct item: use the health insurance comparison to pair the age bracket with the corresponding average figure, without automatically attributing that value to every policyholder.
To avoid confusing the news with other cross-border work topics, this verification remains focused on health insurance premiums in Canton Ticino: it does not add data on permit G, AVS, LPP, refunds, withholding tax or double taxation, which do not appear in the source.
The cross-border reader can thus distinguish what the text measures, that is, percentage increase, average premium and cost composition, from what is not quantified. To carry out this check in a more orderly manner, open comparatore dell'assicurazione malattia.

item.title: CSt: strengthened safeguard clause with incentive tax
item.description: The Council of States has strengthened the safeguard clause for immigration, introducing an incentive tax from 2.000 to 4.000 francs and new indicators.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Council of States strengthens the safeguard clause. - Minimum rates indicated: from 2.000 to 4.000 francs. - New cross-border workers are included among the four national indicators. - Mandatory criminal-record certificate for EU citizens upon arrival.
## Key facts - Body → Council of States - Package → Switzerland-EU stabilization, Bilaterals III - Indicators → net EU immigration, new cross-border workers, unemployment, social assistance - Tax → minimum rates from 2.000 to 4.000 francs - Review → annual - Document → extract from the criminal record - Persons concerned → employees, adult family members, citizens of third countries
The Council of States approved, during its examination of the Switzerland-EU stabilization package, Bilaterals III, a strengthening of the safeguard clause designed to respond to serious economic or social problems linked to excessive immigration. For those working across the border, the most direct reference is the number of new cross-border workers, included among the indicators that can trigger the federal assessment.
The Federal Council should not merely be able to examine the measure. According to the decision of the chamber of cantons, it will have to assess activation when a pre-established national threshold is exceeded in at least one of four areas: net immigration from the EU, new cross-border workers, unemployment or the social assistance rate. The senators also want an annual review of the need to use the clause.
### Tax and corporate responsibility
The most debated new measure is the incentive tax. The majority believes it could encourage employers to give priority to the domestic workforce and promote the arrival of people with high added value. For employees, the levy should be borne by companies; adults joining their family in Switzerland would also be subject to it. The minimum rates indicated range from 2.000 to 4.000 francs, and the proceeds should be distributed to the population. The levy is also envisaged for citizens of third countries, but only after the clause is activated.
Beat Jans acknowledged that an immigration tax would not conflict with the package, while pointing to legal and bureaucratic obstacles. Pascal Broulis expressed opposition, citing the possible burden on sectors with low margins, such as the restaurant industry, and the risk of a similar measure in EU countries for Swiss citizens residing there.
Before this part, the plenary approved the requirement for EU citizens to present an extract from the criminal record upon arrival in Switzerland. The source specifies that a similar practice already exists in Ticino. If the person were considered a danger, the residence permit could be denied or restricted. The chamber of cantons then supported a further tightening of permanent residence rules: unemployed people and recipients of assistance should not be able to submit the application and, for them, the five-year period would restart from zero. In the same session, the federal proposals on land and air transport were approved, with a clarification concerning competition. For a cross-border worker, the decisive distinction is between the parameter used to monitor flows and a personal obligation. The source includes the number of new cross-border workers among the four national values that should prompt an assessment of the clause. It does not, however, establish a numerical threshold, indicate an application date, or describe an automatic measure against every worker who crosses the border. Exceeding one of the values would oblige the Government to take action; the concrete form of the intervention remains tied to the clause and the package under consideration.
### The boundary between flow and individual status
The first level is the flow. The majority links the tax to the goal of pushing companies toward domestic labor and favoring people with high added value. The second level is the party who pays: for employees, the senators identify companies as the payers. The text therefore does not allow one to write that 2.000-4.000 francs would be deducted directly from the paycheck of every cross-border worker: it speaks of minimum rates and the companies' responsibility, not of an individual deduction.
The third level is residence. The source links the extract from the criminal record to the arrival of EU citizens who intend to settle and recalls that the practice is already applied in Ticino. It does not describe a similar check for a mere commute to work. Anyone assessing a residence permit must therefore distinguish work-related mobility from an application to settle.
The same distinction applies to permanent residence. The tightening affecting unemployed people and those receiving social assistance applies to an application for a right of residence; it is not presented as a rule governing the daily crossing of the border. If the application were denied, the five-year period would start over from zero. The source does not clarify how the measure would apply to individual cases already pending.
For the employer, the possible effect is instead organizational: the majority expects an incentive to prioritize domestic labor. Jans points to legal and bureaucratic obstacles; Broulis fears repercussions for sectors with narrow margins. These are political assessments reported by the source, not a definitive calculation of the cost for each company or each cross-border worker.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. A cross-border worker can turn the news into a practical check, without anticipating rules that the source does not establish.
### 1. Separate cross-border work and settlement
The first step is to understand which situation the text describes: the number of new cross-border workers serves as a national indicator, while the criminal record extract and permanent residence concern EU citizens who arrive or request to settle. They are not the same procedure. This distinction prevents automatically interpreting every migration measure as an obligation for those who continue to work across the border.
### 2. If you intend to settle
Anyone preparing to move to Switzerland must consider the criminal record extract among the requirements discussed by the states. The rule approved in the package under consideration provides for its submission by EU citizens upon arrival; if the person poses a danger, the residence permit may be denied or restricted. The source does not indicate the authorities, the format of the extract or the timetable: these are therefore elements that should not be replaced with assumptions.
### 3. If you are applying for permanent residence
Check the condition that the Council of States wanted to tighten. Unemployed people and those receiving assistance should not be able to submit the application; for them, the five-year period for obtaining the right of residence would start again from zero. The measure was challenged by Beat Jans, who considered it incompatible with the free movement of persons: this too indicates that the framework remains linked to the examination of the package.
### 4. If you are an employee
Do not count the amount of 2.000-4.000 francs as a personal deduction. The text assigns the levy to companies for employees, extending it to adults joining their family and, after activation of the clause, to citizens of third countries. However, operating procedures and a start date are missing. For the issue of unemployment, the site offers the guide to disoccupazione frontalieri.
### 5. Follow the process without inventing deadlines
The source refers to an annual review of the clause, but does not provide a deadline for individual workers, a numerical threshold or a payment procedure. The useful check therefore consists of separating what has been approved by the parliamentary body from what will still have to be defined in the implementation. To complete the personal financial check, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Lake Como, body found at 288 meters
item.description: At San Siro, Fire Brigade divers found the body of the 38-year-old who went missing in Lake Como at approximately 288 meters.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Body located at approximately 288 meters deep - Searches concluded in the waters of San Siro - Recovery and transfer of the body to Dongo - Intervention by Fire Brigade divers
## Key facts - Age → 38 years - Location → Lake Como, San Siro - Depth → approximately 288 meters - Equipment → ROV - Destination of the body → Dongo
The search operations for the 38-year-old man missing in the waters of Lake Como, at San Siro, concluded with the body being located at approximately 288 meters deep. The discovery was made possible thanks to Fire Brigade divers and the use of the ROV, an acronym for Remotely Operated Vehicle.
After the location was identified, Fire Brigade specialists proceeded with the recovery. The body was then transferred to Dongo, where it was placed at the disposal of the competent Authority.
The man was a resident of the United Kingdom and of Nepalese origin. The reported sequence includes the search in the lake waters, location using the remotely operated vehicle, recovery and transfer. In the report, the depth is the detail accompanying the outcome of the operation: the body was found at approximately 288 meters and, after it was located, the specialists completed the recovery. The transfer to Dongo marked the final step indicated for the body, now at the disposal of the competent Authority. ## The circumstances of the disappearance
The disappearance dates back to last Monday. The man was on a boat rented in Dongo, where he was sailing with a family with two children, aged 15 and 10. A decisive moment in the voyage occurred in the waters off Acquaseria.
At that point, the 38-year-old man and the 15-year-old boy jumped into the water. The boy then struggled to get back onto the boat and was assisted by his father. Meanwhile, the boat moved away, carried by the current. The man, left in the water, encountered difficulties and disappeared underwater.
The account of the incident sets out the locations and sequence of events: Dongo is the place where the boat had been rented; Acquaseria is the area of water where the dives took place; San Siro is the location identified for the disappearance and subsequent search in Lake Como. The people mentioned are the 38-year-old man, the 15-year-old boy, the father who assisted him, and the 10-year-old child, identified in the source as part of the family.
After the boy struggled to get back onto the boat, the boat moved away while the 38-year-old was still in the water. The source links the man's disappearance underwater to that moment and the subsequent start of the search operations. ## The recovery and transfer
The phase following the location involved recovering the body. The work was carried out by Fire Brigade specialists after the ROV had made it possible to locate the body at approximately 288 meters. The source therefore describes a distinct operational step: the remotely controlled vehicle was used for locating the body, while the specialists carried out the recovery operations.
Once this operation was completed, the body was transferred to Dongo. The same location had been identified as the place where the boat used by the man and the family had been rented. In Dongo, the body was made available to the competent authority, according to reports.
This transfer brings the sequence of reported activities to an end: search in the waters of San Siro, location using an ROV, recovery by the Fire Brigade, and transfer of the body to Dongo. The source does not indicate any further developments, subsequent dates, or other measures. The reported outcome therefore remains that the body was found at approximately 288 meters and the search operations were completed.

## In brief - FIALS Sette Laghi requests more night security - A single guard is stationed at the Emergency Room - Limited access and internal patrols proposed - Intrusions and damaged vending machines reported
## Key facts - Who → FIALS Sette Laghi - Recipient → ASST Sette Laghi - Access points mentioned → Gates on Via Lazio and Viale Borri - Night staffing → A single security guard at the Emergency Room - Requested measures → More staff and periodic patrols - Cited incidents → Damaged and forced-open vending machines
FIALS Sette Laghi has asked ASST Sette Laghi to review the organization of security during night hours at the Varese hospitals. The union brings together three requests: stricter regulation of access, enhanced security, and checks within the facilities. The stated reason is the size and complexity of the hospital, considered incompatible with the presence of a single security guard during the night.
The FIALS company secretariat asks to act before assaults or other critical incidents occur. Therefore, prevention in the proposal does not coincide only with the intervention following a problem, but with an organized presence in the hospital areas.
### Entries to be reviewed
Among the hypotheses indicated is the night closure of access points deemed non-essential. The union specifically cites the gates on Via Lazio and Viale Borri. The stated objective is to leave open only the necessary entrances and ensure effective verification of the people entering the facilities.
> 'A hospital cannot become, during night hours, a place where it is possible to enter and move around without effective verification of access,' states FIALS company secretary Francesco Tucci.
### More extensive security
FIALS also asks ASST to review the organization of the service and, if necessary, the conditions provided for by the contract. The union considers a single guard concentrated in the Emergency Room area insufficient and proposes increasing the number of staff during the night, complementing entrance control with periodic patrols in the various areas of the hospital.
Attention is also paid to those who may be alone in certain services, such as specific laboratories, and to personnel moving from one area to another to transport tests, biological samples, documents, or other material. According to FIALS, a distributed presence should also take into account these internal movements.
The statement recalls episodes of night intrusion during which vending machines were reportedly damaged and forced open. For the union, the value of the damages does not exhaust the problem: the incidents are a signal that requires more prevention. FIALS concludes by asking for a discussion with the workers' representatives on a comprehensive plan for night security in the ASST Sette Laghi hospitals. ## The practical issue: coverage and prevention
The FIALS request can be read as a comparison between a concentrated security presence and broader coverage. In the text, the security guard is described as being in the Emergency Department area; the proposal calls for entrance checks and patrols in the various areas in addition to that post. This is not a decision already adopted by ASST: it is the union's position, which calls for a review of the organization and, if necessary, of the contract.
### Who remains exposed according to the report
The statement distinguishes, without listing specific departments or shifts, two situations. On the one hand, there are workers who may find themselves alone at night in some services, including certain laboratories. On the other, there is staff who must cross the facility to carry tests, biological samples, documents or other material. The practical issue raised by FIALS is therefore the continuity of protection even outside the Emergency Department area.
In this logic, closing a non-essential entrance and monitoring those that remain open are related measures, not alternatives. The first reduces the number of entrances to guard; the second makes checks on people entering the facilities effective. Patrols then add monitoring of internal areas, including those less frequented. This is the organizational scenario put forward by the request, not the announcement of a new service.
The same applies to intrusions. The union cites the damage to the vending machines not only because of the financial cost, but as a possible sign of an unauthorized presence inside the facility. Tucci's point is what could have happened if a worker had found themselves face-to-face with one of the intruders. FIALS uses this question to call for prevention before an assault or serious incident.
For the cross-border reader, the scope should remain clear: the source discusses security in Varese's hospitals and the workers present at night. It does not address Canton Ticino, G permits, AVS or LPP; nor does it cover LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation. There are therefore no grounds for asserting consequences for taxation, social security, health insurance or cross-border employment relationships. On these topics, readers can consult Permesso G/B, the LAMal/CMI guide or the page on ristorni Ticino-Italia, which remain separate from the union's request.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## From the request to the discussion
The source presents a union request, not an operational schedule for employees. The only path explicitly requested is the discussion between ASST Sette Laghi and workers’ representatives. To remain faithful to the statement, the steps can be ordered as follows.
### Four steps indicated by FIALS
1. Assess nighttime access points. The request to ASST is to examine which entrances are essential and which could be closed, with reference to the gates on via Lazio and viale Borri. The request does not say that closure has already been ordered: it presents it as a measure to be assessed.
2. Define the monitoring of entrances that remain open. The objective indicated by the union is to effectively verify the people entering the facilities, preventing access and movement without control during the night.
3. Review security and internal coverage. FIALS asks for more staff during nighttime hours, periodic patrols in the various areas, and attention to services where some workers may find themselves alone. This same point also includes assessing the conditions set out in the security contract, if necessary.
4. Open the discussion on the overall plan. The union asks to discuss with workers’ representatives a project combining regulated access, closure of unnecessary entrances, strengthened security, and internal patrols. In FIALS’s position, the safety of nighttime workers should not depend on chance.
This sequence distinguishes a union request from a measure that has actually been approved. The source text does not communicate ASST decisions, implementation timelines, or results already achieved. The process therefore remains the one indicated by FIALS: discussing an overall plan with the company and representatives.
To explore aspects unrelated to hospital security, separate tools are needed. The news item does not provide tax or salary data; for a separate payslip check, use calcolatore stipendio.
